page: Microsoft Azure D48als_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dalv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, though it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core capabilities. The server achieved top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core testing and strong performance in stress-ng CPU evaluations. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for small cached blocks but drop to average levels for large uncached read and write blocks. In database operations, the server demonstrates strong performance, executing 66.68 million Redis SET operations per second. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speed is top-tier for text generation with small models, but drops to weak performance levels when processing large 70B models due to memory constraints.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48als_v6 offers high compute density with its 48 dedicated vCPUs, making it a resource-dense option for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and the complete absence of local storage. This configuration is suited for CPU-bound workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, ray tracing, and small-scale LLM inference, whereas it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale AI model execution.
